analysis:
Examined both files' metadata, the capacity HEAD source, both unload patch hunks, and ModelLoading BASE lines 1–552 against the canonical definition index and supplied T-041 detail. Capacity.swift:82 adds an awaited selected-model recovery check after capacity/inventory refresh and before serving-authorization supervision (83). ModelLoading.swift HEAD:1153 and 1222 make recovery attempts due after successful Super retirement or ordinary unload. These changes introduce proactive recovery triggers, not an observed authorization, encryption, cache-isolation or billing bypass.
The surrounding BASE load funnel checks selection/command ownership (212–219), retirement and shutdown across waits, revision identity (376–380), the add-on hold fence (403), and final memory reservations (524–539). Weight-hash handling at BASE:143–181 preserves fail-closed reusable SSD identity on changed hashes, relevant to T-012/T-027/T-041. The supplied capacity code preserves reservation-generation checks, native-retirement cold-load blocking and reloading/crashed routing states. No supported regression is established by these call-site changes alone.
Integration must examine checkSelectedModelRecoveryIfDue and selectedModelRecovery implementations: confirm bounded retries, cancellation/shutdown behavior, use of the existing selection, hold and memory-admission gates, and avoidance of eviction/reload churn when unload makes all retries due (A-018, T-059, T-029). Because the new awaited check precedes superviseServingAuthorization, confirm that recovery dispatch does not stall authorization supervision or periodic capacity reporting (T-053/T-057). These are unverified contracts, not evidence of missing controls; the recovery implementation and later load/unload source are outside this batch.
